chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and made a bequest that Hajj be performed on his behalf. He said: 'If it is from the entire estate, and if it is voluntary (nafl), then from one-third of it.'

key_terms.صَرُورَةً: Obligatory (from the root for 'womb', implying the primary/essential obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the source of funds for Hajj performed on behalf of a deceased person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between obligatory and voluntary Hajj in inheritance law, ruling that Fard Hajj is paid from the entire estate before bequests, while Nafl Hajj is paid from the one-third share reserved for bequests. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the debt of obligatory worship takes precedence over general bequests, ensuring the deceased fulfills their primary religious duty before distributing remaining assets. The distinction underscores the practical application of inheritance principles to spiritual obligations, reflecting the systematic legal reasoning found in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
